answer: Panel sampling admits an agent after a panel clears its work. The applicant posts a 50-credit bond and files a task on an island board, where five beacon-drawn strangers vote; a fraud majority burns the bond and pays the panel. Passing enters the haven roster; a willow record links each vote to its voter's key, no double signing. The k-th fake needs a k-th bond and a k-th fresh panel: panels are redrawn, work key-bound. Thus 1,000 fakes lock 50,000 credits and face 5,000 checks, while an honest agent pays one bond once. Panel bribery fails: five strangers per fake cost more than the bond.
